## Scenario

> A university wants an Online Student Advising System so students can request academic advising, view advisor availability, schedule appointments, and receive advising notes. Actors: Student, Academic Advisor, and Administrator. Key high-level functions: submit advising request, check advisor schedules, book/reschedule/cancel an appointment, and view/download advising notes.

## Instruction
1. Create a Use Case Diagram in (e.g. Lucidchart or Draw.io) showing actors and main use cases (e.g., Submit Request, View Advisor Availability, Book Appointment, Reschedule/Cancel Appointment, Upload/View Advising Notes, Admin: Manage Advisors/Schedules).
2. Create a Activity Diagram in (e.g. Lucidchart or Draw.io) describing the workflow for “Student books an advising appointment” from start to finish include decision points (e.g., advisor available?), parallel actions (notify advisor + update calendar), and end states.
3. Submit diagrams as PNG or PDF and include a 200–300 word explanation for each diagram describing your assumptions.

# Use Case Diagram

![](data:image/png;base64,)
- The Use Case Diagram shows the scope and user interactions inside the Online Student Advising system across 3 primary factors being the "Student", the "Academic Advisor, and the "Administrator".
- The student is the primary end user who starts core self-service functions, including submitting advising requests, viewing advisor free time, making appointments, rescheduling or cancelling existing appointments and also viewing or downloading advising notes.
- The Academic Advisor will interact with the system to review schedules, access student records and also upload official advising notes to following sessions.
- Lastly, the Administrator maintains system infrastructure by managing advisor profiles, roster assignments and also operational availability schedules.
  

# Activity Diagram

![](data:image/png;base64,)
- Some Key design assumptions control this structure.
- The first being, user authentication is considered as a prerequisite for all interaction.
- actors must securely log in before accessing all or any features, keeping security concerns small rather than cluttering the functional diagram.
- Second, data access must be strictly controlled by role-based permissions to ensure privacy.
- Students need to only possess read-only permissions for their personal advising notes, and Advisers are granted edit access to upload their notes only for their assigned advice. 
- Third, system updates such as appointment bookings or cancellations will automatically trigger notification services to keep both sites be it students and advisors be informed without needing secondary actor interaction.
- and finally, administrative control over advisor schedules establishes the baseline operational hours in which individual advisors can setup their availability-
